## What you did

- You traced Orbitly's ~8% iOS funnel drop to your own SDK: kestrel-ios 3.2.0 sends `event_id` as a per-session counter, so #240's event_id-only dedupe discarded ~1.18M legitimate events (≈8.1% of their iOS volume); Zest's pilot app lost 3,812 events too [1].
- You fixed the dedupe key to `(project_id, device_id, event_id)` — replays are still dropped — with tests green and lint clean, and opened PR #247 with Maya as reviewer [1][2].

## What changed

- Maya approves the logic and will merge once CI is green, but she wants the number of dropped Orbitly events for Thursday's call — you already have it (≈1.18M) [2].
- Noa finalized the 12/11 postmortem and will present it at Friday's incident review [3].
- CI now runs Go 1.23.4 (#245, merged, no code change) [4].
- Rachel confirmed Zest's dashboards are complete again and is closing their ticket [6].

## What is still open

- PR #247 awaits Maya's merge; once deployed, run the replay from landing for Orbitly from 13/11 (~40 min) and Zest (seconds), then check `ingest_dedupe_dropped_total` for Orbitly stays near zero — the replay must not run before deployment [1][2].
- You owe the team a note to the iOS team asking them to restore UUID `event_id` in 3.2.1 — a draft is ready [1].
- From incident-review prep: add an alert for the ingest dead-letter queue above 1,000 messages before Friday [7].
